$comment: DECLARED translation scope per coverage tier. Hand-authored, version-controlled.
This is the 'declared' half of the launch gate in I18N-PLAN.md section 1; the 'actual'
half is i18n/coverage.json, which is generated from disk. A locale may join
i18n.locales only when (declared - covered) is empty for its tier.
Route strings are canonical, trailing-slash, locale-STRIPPED. All 40 core routes were
validated against the live sitemap on 2026-08-09.
Tier ASSIGNMENT per locale lives in i18n/locales.config.ts (field: coverage).
This file owns the route SETS only. One writer per file, per section 17.
The first 9 routes of 'micro' are the global-chrome closure floor: every route reachable
from navbar, footer, and MegaMenu. Removing any of them fails the locale build
(onBrokenLinks: 'throw'). See section 4 Phase 2 task (b).
A routeSets entry has ONE OF THREE value shapes, and the manifest builder must handle all
three: (1) the string '*' meaning every route on the site; (2) an array of explicit
canonical routes; (3) a DERIVED object {base, excludeRouteGlobs, retainRoutes} as used by
'full-minus-course-leaves'. Shape 3 arrived with version 2; that is what the bump records.
Tier B scope, locked as decision 4 in section 18: the full site MINUS the 71
docs/courses leaves, with all 7 category hubs RETAINED. ~190 - 71 = ~119 routes.
Expressed as a derivation rather than 119 hand-listed routes on purpose: an enumerated
copy of 'full' would silently rot the first time an English page is added, and the
whole point of this entry is that it tracks the site automatically.
SEMANTICS, stated exactly so the Phase 2 manifest builder cannot misread them:
base              name of another routeSet to start from. '*' here means every route.
excludeRouteGlobs canonical, trailing-slash, locale-STRIPPED route globs. '*' matches
exactly ONE path segment and NEVER crosses a '/'. There is no '**'.
retainRoutes      applied AFTER the excludes; retain always wins over exclude. It is
a belt-and-braces guard, not decoration.
Why the glob is leaf-shaped: a category hub is docs/courses/<topic>/index.mdx and
renders at /docs/courses/<topic>/ (ONE segment after /courses/), while a leaf is
docs/courses/<topic>/<leaf>.mdx and renders at /docs/courses/<topic>/<leaf>/ (TWO).
So a single-segment-wildcard glob at depth two hits leaves only. Verified 2026-08-11:
71 leaves, 7 hubs, and no leaf overrides its slug, so no leaf collapses to hub depth.
A source-path glob such as 'docs/courses/*/*' would be WRONG here: it also matches
docs/courses/<topic>/index.mdx and would delete the hubs this entry exists to keep.
Promotion path: a Tier B locale earns its course leaves once its category hubs clear
500 impressions/month in GSC. That promotion is a one-word edit to that locale's
'coverage' in i18n/locales.config.ts ('full'), never an edit to this entry.
React .tsx routes translated via code.json only. They can never be 'covered' by a
translated markdown file, so the manifest builder injects them into EVERY locale so
they stay in the hreflang cluster. This is the one accepted exception to invariant 4;
without it the locale homepage loses its alternates entirely.
English-only in every locale, replaced by a localized one-line notice. Translated
legal text creates real exposure and has zero SEO value (section 1). Requires a
plugin-content-pages exclude AND footer link replacement in non-en locales, or the
footer alone throws in every locale (section 4 Phase 2 task (d)).
